chapters.title: Chapter 151: Avery Thoughts
paragraphs: "Yes, yes, let’s get some KFC, enjoy the air conditioning, and leave quickly."
"Look at how shabby he looks. He probably has no money left in his pocket after buying the phone. You two, don’t go too far."
"Let’s go, handsome Brother!"
Ojhaka giggled, linked arms with Fatty, and strutted away, heading straight into a Chanel boutique.
Avery was a little upset. She stamped her foot and said, "You stupid Bunny, how can you just tolerate this?!"
"She’s spending her own money earned from selling her body. Why bother arguing with her?"
Though Leah’s words sounded reasonable, it was obvious she also felt somewhat unwilling.
Luis took their hands, one on each side, and said with a smile, "What’s there to be afraid of? Let’s go too. This is the perfect excuse for your Brother to buy you bags."
Avery cheered, giving him a seductive look as she said, "Brother, I want to use an advance on my ’selling my body’ money."
"You silly Avery, what nonsense are you talking about? What’s all this about selling your body for money?!"
"That’s my business. If you have any conscience, Bunny, you should give Brother some benefits later... Hehehe!!"
Luis said generously, "Come on, today your Brother will let you show off too. Don’t hold back later."
Swaggering into the store, Ojhaka and Fatty were looking at a new pink bag. It was very small and clearly designed for young girls, and she seemed to like it a bit.
Seeing the three walk in, Ojhaka said sarcastically, "Really, these paupers can’t even read. They dare to walk into any place."
Fatty immediately chimed in, "Even if they can’t afford it, they can still look. Maybe they’ll stubbornly put it on a credit card or take out an online loan. It’s not impossible."
"Young people are full of passion. Sometimes they do stupid things just to prove a point. It’s understandable."
Once inside the store, the two girls were clearly a bit uncomfortable. After all, it was their first time in such a luxury boutique.
"Madam, you have excellent taste. This is a new small backpack from the series, perfect for young girls traveling light."
The shopping guide immediately said to Ojhaka, "Now is the best time to buy with a 20% discount.
When Ojhaka saw the price, she noticed it was still over 4,000 dollars even after the discount. She immediately muttered, "Why are your new designs getting more and more expensive?"
"Madam, this collection is meticulously crafted..."
The Fatty beside her frowned. Although Chanel is very famous, aside from limited editions and some classic commemorative pieces, many of their bags are priced around 1,000 or 2,000 dollars.
Last night, he said it would cost a few thousand for several sessions—one blowjob and two anal sessions—and Fatty’s budget couldn’t exceed 3,000 dollars.
Ojhaka was also struggling with this. They had agreed that any money left after buying the bag would be her allowance. Her goal was to pick one that cost just over 1,000 dollars and pocket the rest.
"This new design isn’t even that nice!"
Fatty immediately spoke up. He didn’t want to be a sucker.
The shopping guides in these kinds of places have sharp eyes. They like seeing young girls bring older men in, but they also know these situations often don’t end well.

So-called sugar daddies sponsor one woman after another, and their calculations are extremely shrewd. It was obvious this wasn’t just a passionate fling anymore—Fatty was getting tired of it and would definitely be stingy with his spending.
"Then take your time looking around at other styles. If you need anything, just call me directly."
The shopping guide had a keen eye. She smiled professionally and walked over to Luis.
Fanning the flames and stirring up confrontation—this kind of drama was the most entertaining. Once tempers flared, it was normal for men to splurge just to save face.
The shopping guide came over and said with a smile, "Sir, madam, would you like me to introduce some items to you?"
"Avery, Leah, if you like any, just tell me directly."
Luis patted each of them on the butt and said confidently, "Pick whatever you like. Don’t worry about the price.
"Okay, Brother!"
The two girls were a bit intimidated seeing that the prices here started at five figures, but this act of taking advantage gave them courage.
Leah wasn’t one to be bullied. She immediately said, "That series bag is new, right? I want to see it."
"Okay!"
The shopping guide brought them over and began introducing the items in the store.
Ojhaka was a little angry when she saw this and whispered, "Godfather, they’re doing this on purpose."
Thinking about the price, Fatty immediately said, "We agreed last night it would only be 3,000 dollars. Why don’t you look at something else?"
Hearing this, Ojhaka said angrily, "Godfather, at most I’ll serve you well in the future. I can’t lose face now. Besides, it’s your reputation on the line too."

Fatty was, at best, comfortably off—not a rich man—and he didn’t have much extra money. More importantly, he didn’t want to invest any more in her. The only reason he gave her a thousand at a time was because she agreed to anal.
Now that he’d had her in all three holes, she naturally wasn’t worth as much. Expecting to sell her at a high price was a pipe dream. He was already getting a bit tired of her.
"Don’t be impatient, stay calm. They’re just stalling for time. There’s no way they’ll actually buy anything."
Fatty was also stalling. He didn’t want to waste his money again. A budget of 4,000 dollars spent on another student girl would be enough to make her fall for him.
"That’s right!"
Ojhaka thought it made sense. She sneered and walked over, saying, "Stop pretending. This beautiful model is 5,000 dollars after discount. You should take a good look at it."
The shopping guide saw that Luis was getting a little angry. Although he was dressed plainly, she didn’t discriminate at all and immediately began introducing the best bags in the series.
It had a girly style and couldn’t hold much, but it was very small and pretty. After the 20% discount, it was just over 4,900 dollars, practically no different from 5,000 dollars.
Ojhaka came over purely to force the issue. Leah immediately showed hesitation, and Avery also seemed a bit at a loss.
Although Avery was still a virgin, she was also vain and knew a lot of gossip. Just from observing Ojhaka, she already understood the situation.

chapters.title: Chapter 152: Stingy Only With Myself
paragraphs: "It really is quite nice!"
Luis came over and asked, "Is this the most expensive model in this series?"
"Yes!"
The shopping guide could already smell the scent of success from his understated tone.
Luis directly took out his card and handed it to her, saying with a smile, "Two, in stock. Place the order first!"
"Okay!"
The shopping guide was delighted. He had judged correctly.

When she went to the counter to swipe the card, the fat man said sarcastically, "Brother, don't push yourself too hard. You don't look well off. How long will it take you to pay back the 10,000 dollar credit card bill you just swiped?"
"These two girls are indeed pretty, but they're not worth that much. You'd better calm down."
Luis looked at him coldly and said, "In my heart, they are priceless treasures. Their value cannot be measured with money. Spending this money to make them happy is the most important thing to me."
The salesgirl was also particularly skilled at stirring up trouble. She immediately brought over the order slip and the POS machine, saying, "Sir, your savings card has been swiped. Please sign."
"Thank you!"
When she mentioned the savings card, she emphasized the word, making it clear. She was such a clever and likable person, making the spending experience feel comfortable.
After Luis signed, he said, "Pack these two first. I'll take a look at the others."

This scene had already made the fat man feel somewhat discouraged, but Ojhaka was unhappy. She felt particularly irritated seeing the way Leah and Avery looked at each other after their surprise, then glanced at her.
She secretly tugged at the fat man's sleeve and said, "Godfather, please, I want one too. At most, I'll listen to you from now on in how we play."
How to play? Every part of your body has already been played with by me.
But the fat man remembered something and gritted his teeth, saying, "Introduce your sister to me, and I'll add another 2,000 dollars to your budget."
"Fuck you, my sister is two years younger than me."
Ojhaka was trembling with anger. She hadn't expected this disgusting fat man to already have his eyes on her sister after just one meeting.

The fat man said righteously, "What's wrong with being younger? Looking at her flirtatious demeanor, she's not a virgin anyway. Hanging out with hoodlums every day—what's the difference between being played for free by others and being played by me?
"I'll give you another 1,000 dollars, making it 6,000 dollars total. Both of you can keep me company..."
With that one sentence, Ojhaka's anger completely vanished. When she thought of Leah and Avery's arrogant and domineering attitudes, her mind filled with wicked thoughts.
Indeed, her sister wasn't a virgin anymore. If she was going to be played around with anyway, she might as well get something out of it. Giving her a few thousand would make her ecstatic.
"Okay!"
Driven by her inner demons, Ojhaka immediately shouted loudly, "I want one of these bags too!"
The shopping guide smiled and immediately arranged for the card to be swiped. This was the situation she most wanted to see. Once the competition was stirred up, it was her victory.
"Only 1,000 dollars left. Let's go. I'll give you the money later," the fat man whispered after swiping his card. "Ask your sister out tonight. Don't delay, or you'll regret it."
"Got it!"
After buying the 5,000 dollar bag, Ojhaka's mood improved, and she was already thinking about how to show off.

On the other side, Luis had already calmed the two little girls down and was trying hair clips with them, even though they were still feeling uneasy. He said with a smile, "School is troublesome. You can't wear jewelry, but hair clips should be fine."
"Sir, this is the new Butterfly Loves Flower series. It's only 950 dollars after the discount..."
"I'll take them. Pack one for each of them first. We'll settle the bill together later."
"Yes, sir."
Ojhaka's anger instantly flared up again. "Godfather, I want one too!!"
"Damn it!!"
The fat man gritted his teeth and swiped his card again, but there wasn't much balance left.
After he finished, Luis took the two girls to look at Chanel slippers. Yes, the slippers were exquisitely designed and cost over 800 dollars a pair.
"Godfather, let's go!"
Ojhaka wasn't stupid. She took the fat man's arm and left with him in a triumphant manner.

The shopping guide smiled disdainfully. He really was just an ordinary person with a bit of dirty money. What was he trying to prove? Spending over 5,000 dollars in a luxury store barely qualified him as average.
While she was still lost in thought, the voice from the other side was even more piercing:
"Pack these two crystal hair ties as well!"
"Brother in law, these aren't practical. They're uncomfortable to wear."
"Ah... then these earrings are nice too."
"Brother in law..."
"It's only 1,000 dollars. That's cheap. Take two. See if there's anything else you like."

After leaving the store, the two little girls were somewhat dazed. Each carried several gift bags. Aside from the bags, they had spent a considerable amount on various items. On average, each of them had spent 10,000 dollars.
The shopping guide was already beaming with joy. Luis cheerfully took them upstairs and treated them to lunch at the most expensive Japanese restaurant.
"Brother in law, can these be returned?"
Leah was almost going crazy. Spending 5,000 dollars on a bag was clearly beyond her usual means.
Avery also looked up, her eyes complex—a mix of approval and reluctance. This was the first time in her life she had encountered the concept of luxury goods.
Luis took in their expressions, thought for a moment, and said, "Keep them all. This is a gift from your brother in law."
"But this..."
Leah was very worried. She knew her second sister was frugal. If she found out about this...
"Don't worry. Just don't tell your second sister!"
Luis looked at the menu and smiled softly. "Your brother in law is usually stingy, but he's absolutely generous to you. Besides, I'm not as poor as you think."
"I'm willing to spend money on my precious Leah. I'm just stingy with myself."
When Avery heard this, she said, "Brother in law, then you wouldn't be willing to spend money on me!"
"You're also a treasure in your brother in law's heart. How could I be stingy with you?"
Luis reached out and gently touched Avery's cheek in front of his sister in law.
Leah was obviously a little jealous but didn't make a scene. She just snorted, flipped through the menu, and glanced outside. "They just won't go away."

chapters.title: Chapter 153: Suspicious Nancy
paragraphs: Even if you're a virgin, unless some big boss specifically wants to take your virginity and is willing to pay a high price for a girl with a certain birth date, the going rate is really only around 1,000 or 2,000 dollars.
She wasn't shameless enough to ask for such a high price. Moreover, her relationship with Luis had been warming up lately, and she didn't want to ruin her image in his eyes.
Even if it was a romantic relationship, it was better to make it long-term rather than constantly switching partners like Ojhaka...
As she was speaking, Ojhaka walked in, and the heavyset man was no longer beside her.
She glanced at how the three of them were sitting. Luis was on one side, and the two girls were sitting together on the other.
She immediately sneered. "Yes, there are set meals outside. Let's just leave quickly after eating."
After saying that, she took the middle seat.
When paying the bill, she looked at them with contempt. Although the fat man had left impatiently, she firmly believed Luis was just pretending to be rich.

The biggest feature of this restaurant was its self-service grill and seafood bar. If you didn't have much money, you could sit outside, order a couple of dishes for $15 or $20, and leave. Normally, the cost of eating there wasn't high.
"Hello, I saw some lobsters when I walked in, right?"
Luis stopped the two girls and waved to call the manager over.
The manager chuckled and said, "Yes, but the lobster and prime cuts aren't part of the all-you-can-eat buffet."
The implication was clear. Although the buffet here was famous, if you really had money, you would still order the premium seafood separately instead of just eating the set meals.
Luis walked to the front of the tank and looked at the lively lobsters, king crab legs, and striped bass swimming inside.
He said, "These are the ones I want."
"Okay, sir, let me first explain the market price of the bass—"
Luis handed over his card and said unhappily, "Did I ask you the price?
"I'm sorry, sir. I'll arrange it for you right away."
"Bring me everything in this tank," Luis said firmly.

Ojhaka was close enough to hear the manager swipe the card and hand it back. "Sir, the wild striped bass weighs four pounds, total price $320. With the discount, we'll include two bowls of lobster bisque for free."
"You're not trying to switch it for some cheaper fish, are you?"
"Of course not, sir. This is the real thing."
The $40 buffet versus the $1,000 seafood feast for three people — the difference was obvious.
Ojhaka didn't even take a few bites before slamming the door and leaving with a dark face. Leah and Avery were laughing so hard they nearly choked.
But Leah also felt a little distressed. She had spent a huge amount for her.
If her second sister or mother found out, they'd probably kill her.
When Leah got home, she ran back to her room like a thief. She'd already decided that if her mother or second sister asked, she would say it was a knockoff.

That afternoon, Nancy took Lily to a spa and salon. It had to be said that when it came to pampering, it was the elder sister who led the way. Now, under her influence, Lily had begun to think that women should dress up for themselves. In the past, she would never have been willing to spend the money.
Anyway, so many nice things were bought, and the two girls were smiling happily. Their laughter could be heard downstairs.
"Brother-in-law, my eldest sister asked us to go downstairs to wash our hair and do a facial mask."
Before Luis could think of anything mischievous, Leah ran out with Avery.

Luis smiled helplessly and played on the computer the whole afternoon. In the evening, Lily didn't dare drive, so she took a taxi to send them back to school. Luis was puzzled but couldn't do anything.
"Why did you buy such an expensive bag for Leah?"
Nancy came back first and said sternly, "She's still a student. If her mother knew, she'd scold you to death."
"It's just a replica."
Luis naturally cooperated with the lie.

Nancy's face hardened. "You can fool Lily, but you can't fool me. This is the latest model of a designer girl's bag. I've been seeing it in my friends' posts. Counterfeits haven't even hit the market yet.
"Besides, I saw the invoice."
Nancy's eyes flashed as she asked sharply, "Even if Lily doesn't know the value of other things, I do. Those crystal hair ties and jewelry aren't cheap."
Facing her questioning, Luis rolled his eyes. "Sister, I'm buying things for your sister. It's not that serious, right?"
"You haven't bought anything this expensive for Lily, so why would you buy one for her little sister? And why does Avery have one too?"
Nancy narrowed her eyes and gritted her teeth. "Are you planning something bad?"
Ever since she'd crossed a certain line with Luis, their relationship had been tangled and confusing.
Nancy didn't know why she was so angry. Was she angry that her brother-in-law was spoiling her sister? Or was she simply jealous?
The more Nancy thought about it, the sadder she became. It would be one thing if only her sister had the bag — but why Avery too?
Faced with her aggressive questioning, Luis smiled faintly. "Big sister, you guessed it right. I'm just bribing you. I'm just being attentive."

After going downstairs, Luis saw no car at the entrance of the community, so he made a phone call.
"I'm free right now, just driving around. Take a taxi yourself. For late night snacks, go to Aunt Fatty's place for barbecue."
Nancy said this impatiently and hung up the phone immediately.
At that moment, she was gripping the steering wheel, her mood extremely foul. Having waited at the entrance for half an hour, she, who was prone to overthinking, was already filled with rage.

She was impatient, and Luis was equally impatient. After hanging up, he indeed hailed a taxi.
However, he didn't go to the barbecue place she specified. Instead, he went to the back gate of the park at the end of the road, to a particularly famous street food stall: casserole chicken.

None of the women in the Wood family ate chicken prepared this way, especially Nancy with her self-righteous, sanctimonious attitude. Luis's good mood had been completely ruined by her, so naturally, he wasn't going to indulge her bad habits anymore.
Missions, favorability meter... To hell with it. It's not like hers is the only mission line. At worst, I'll just ignore you.
"Where are you?"
"Eating!"
"Didn't I say to eat barbecue at Aunt Fatty's place?"
"Then you go eat. Send me the bill for reimbursement."

After saying that, Luis hung up the phone. Just then, the casserole chicken was served. Hot charcoal burned beneath the pot, and as the chicken stew bubbled, its aroma wafted up—a smell most people couldn't tolerate.
Those who could sit here were regulars. Nancy parked her car and walked straight over.
The sister-in-law wore a white sleeveless vest, a pair of black denim shorts, and flip-flop style mid-heeled sandals.

These were all clothes belonging to his Mother-in-law and Lily. She hadn't brought any of her own clothes over. Yet, even dressed like this, she carried herself like a supermodel, walking with such style that everyone present was drawn to her.
With her tall, devilish figure, she'd look stunning even in a sack. Combined with her striking beauty, it was impossible not to notice her.
"Are you doing this on purpose?"
As soon as Nancy sat down, her face looked somewhat unpleasant.

Luis took a sip of the standard local liquor and said nonchalantly, "Big sister, what business is it of yours what I eat for a late-night snack? I don't feel like barbecue, what's wrong with wanting chicken?"
Nancy was momentarily speechless.
Luis continued eating the meat and drank some wine, saying, "If you don't want to eat it, big sister, just eat something else. It's not a big deal."
"Your nerve is growing bigger and bigger. Since when do you speak so disrespectfully?"
Nancy was so angry she slapped the table.
Luis raised his head and looked at her coldly, saying, "If you're not happy about it, big sister, you can leave. I never said I have to please you."
Nancy was furious: "Is this a challenge? You really think I won't tell your wife?"
"Whether you tell her or not is irrelevant. I never cared."
Luis picked up a piece of chicken tail and started eating it, sneering, "It's you I'm curious about. You're as controlling as Mom. I wonder why you're exerting so much effort on me."
"I'm your sister-in-law, can't I say anything?"
Nancy's voice suddenly rose.

Luis, however, looked at her calmly and said softly, "A married daughter is like spilled water. However good your life is after marriage is your own affair. What have you bought for your sisters? Have you been able to support your father, or my Mother-in-law, your own mother?"
Hearing this, Nancy was momentarily taken aback.
Luis continued drinking and eating his food, speaking lightly:
Luis continued drinking and eating his food, speaking lightly:
"I know you look down on me, a live-in son-in-law. But just like your worthless husband, I didn't pay much of a bride price, right? Did that good-for-nothing of yours contribute any money?
"But me? The water card, electricity card, broadband, natural gas—I'm the one paying for all of it. Tell me, big sister, have you ever even seen these cards?"
Nancy felt extremely guilty at this point. Not only had she never seen such things at her natal home, but even when she was married, it was her in-laws who handled all those payments.
Nancy said stubbornly, "What does that prove?"
"A married daughter is like spilled water!"

Luis took a fierce gulp of wine, put down his glass, and asked, "Big sister, you all used to laugh at me for being a live-in son-in-law, but I've shouldered the responsibilities I should have in this household."
"You, on the other hand, don't even know how much the annual property fees are for this family. What right do you have to criticize me?"
This made Nancy a bit flustered, but she still gritted her silver teeth and said, "Don't be so harsh. You are a live-in son-in-law, that's a fact."
Luis sneered, "Right. Between the two sons-in-law, I'm the more disgraceful one. But I pay for your family's water, electricity, gas, and Leah's school expenses."
"What about your rich second-generation husband? Aside from acting pretentious all day, has he ever spent a single cent?"
"I became a live-in son-in-law because I love Lily, not to be looked down upon by you all."

Luis took another fierce sip of wine, then sneered, "At first, I thought this brother-in-law was alright, and that you, big sister, were doing well. But then I realized, what does it have to do with us?"
"You complain daily about the wine at home being bad, yet I've never seen you bring a bottle. You mock Mom's handbags, yet I've never seen you buy her one."
"Let me tell you straight, I look down on you right now. Don't even talk about being poor now; even if you had money, you wouldn't spend it on your own mother."
Hearing this, Nancy was already panicking internally and lost her confidence. She said, "It's not like there's anything at home that requires spending money."

Luis knew her attitude was softening and immediately changed his approach, saying, "There are expenses everywhere. Firewood, rice, oil, salt—every little thing costs money. If I hadn't been subsidizing the family all these years, where do you think Mom would get the money to play cards every day?"
"Enough, big sister. You always want to control me now. I just want to ask one question: what gives you the right?"

Luis laughed coldly, "Just because you come home every day to show off? You're the eldest sister of the family. Forget that you're married now; even before you married, what did you contribute to the family?"

He really felt like getting up to see how his sister-in-law would act around him today, but if his mother-in-law was there, he lost interest.
"It’s just, your mother-in-law is coming over tonight.
About today’s matter, give me a definite answer.
"Don’t worry, Mom.
I already said it was a scam call.
Daniel is just making trouble for no reason."
"That bastard, he slapped me last time and just doesn’t want to apologize.
He’s deliberately being unreasonable to try and muddy the waters.
No way."
"Really?"
"Really, I’m heading out first."
Nancy’s voice was light and breezy, the kind that was refreshing and carried a delicate softness.
If she had been in her previous hysterical, irritable state, they’d probably be arguing again by now.
Last night, at the critical moment, Luis had honestly let her calculate the total.
She honestly confessed all the money she owed.
When they added it up, even she was shocked.
She remembered it was 21,500 dollars.
After just a week, with penalties included, it was nearly 23,000 dollars.
The more Nancy thought about it, the more horrified she became.
At this rate, even if she really had to sell her body, she wouldn’t be able to pay off the snowballing interest.
It was truly a vicious cycle designed to consume people whole without a trace.
At that moment, she was exceptionally vulnerable in Luis’s arms.
Her gaze grew even softer as she watched the man transfer 30,000 dollars.
Besides shame, there was also gratitude, because Luis added one more thing, "Big sister, you’re not even carrying your bag, you must have sold it.
Go buy a new, better one tomorrow.
Don’t let your mother-in-law laugh at you."
"And also, go get a facial, pamper yourself a little.
Be radiant, let them see how well you’re doing now."
The sister-in-law said "Okay," tacitly agreeing.
She felt a little pleased that her brother-in-law was so attentive and observed things so carefully, never imagining that a powerful external plugin meant she had no privacy whatsoever.
Nancy was still thinking with shame, ’My brother-in-law noticed so many details, he must have had his eyes on my body for a long time...’
If it weren’t for this particular family relationship, just based on how much he cared about her and his willingness to spend money so generously, she would be willing to be his lover, his mistress.
At that moment, Sister-in-Law Nancy: Favorability Meter 80%
The sound of the main door closing rang out.
Luis turned over and continued sleeping.
There were plenty of opportunities to be alone with his mother-in-law.
Having ejaculated three times last night, his energy was depleted, and he needed proper rest.
His mother-in-law’s voluptuous body was naturally full of allure, but he would hold back until a mission was issued.
The top priority was figuring out how to increase her favorability meter.
Given their current relationship, his mother-in-law was like meat already in his mouth.
He was just waiting for the moment he craved it most to devour her, that would be truly satisfying.

chapters.title: Chapter 168: Daniel’s Family Arrival
paragraphs: Around 5 PM, when Ruth returned home, she felt slightly ashamed, "Son-in-law, you’ve worked hard. Let Mom give you a hand."
Luis in the kitchen was wearing shorts and had deliberately put on a vest, busily preparing dinner inside and out.

Ruth was dressed very beautifully today. A small, finely patterned floral dress accentuated her mature, full curves. Though she wasn’t wearing makeup, that natural charm was her most captivating quality.

When people are poor, constantly calculating every penny for daily necessities makes them worldly and irritable. But now, free from those pressures and living a comfortable life, her temperament had instead softened considerably. Especially in front of Luis, she was completely a little woman, showing a trend towards becoming like Lily.
"Mom, it’s fine, don’t trouble yourself. I can handle it."
Luis washed his hands, then suddenly wrapped his arms around her waist. Ruth revealed a girlishly shy expression, enchanted by her son-in-law’s loving, affectionate gaze.
"Mom, you’re so beautiful!"
Luis kissed her. She closed her eyes, slightly parted her cherry lips, and actively met his kiss, sucking on her son-in-law’s tongue.
At this stage, the final step was surely a matter of course. Luis was full of anticipation, not knowing when he would be able to freely taste this voluptuous body.

By the time the door opened again, the two had already separated. Ruth was wiping the dining table, Luis continued bustling in the kitchen as if nothing had happened, yet it all seemed particularly harmonious.
"Mom, we’re back."
Lily and Nancy had met downstairs and came up together, chatting and laughing. It’s just that Nancy felt quite guilty in her heart whenever she looked at her younger sister.

The only consolation was that her younger sister had permitted her brother-in-law to stray. There was no actual physical infidelity between her and her brother-in-law, but what if her younger sister found out about the things her older sister and her husband had done? Would she fly into a rage? The thought made her extremely anxious.

She no longer wielded the authoritative air of the eldest sister acting like a mother. Instead, she was very considerate, constantly telling her younger sister to rest well and take care of the baby in her belly.
"Hubby, you’ve worked hard..."
Lily entered the kitchen and hugged Luis. Luis said with a helpless expression, "I’m all dirty, don’t hug me."
"Nothing’s dirty about you. Hubby smells the best."

After saying that, she playfully raised her head, pouted her little lips, closed her eyes with an expectant look. Luis held her and gave her a very lingering, wet kiss right in front of his mother-in-law and sister-in-law.

Now Lily has tasted the happiness of being treated as a treasure by her whole family, so she is particularly relaxed and dares to kiss passionately in public. If it were her previous introverted and dull personality, she would absolutely never have dared.
Because her mother would scold her, her elder sister would scold her, and once they found something displeasing, all sorts of old-fashioned and feudal reasons would come out.

But now her mother-in-law, Ruth, is watching happily. Even though the relationship with her son-in-law is already quite absurd, as a mother, she is simply delighted to see her daughter and son-in-law being so loving.
After being alerted to the sense of crisis by her eldest daughter, she suddenly found her feelings of guilt and sinfulness weren’t so severe anymore.

She thought to herself, with such an excellent son-in-law, rather than having his soul snatched away by some vixen outside, it would be better for her to substitute for her daughter in serving her husband, resolving the son-in-law’s desires during this period so he can stay at home contentedly.
Nancy could never have imagined that the report she made, intended to warn her mother and sister, instead ended up providing psychological counseling for her mother-in-law, Ruth.
"You two are an old married couple now, please be considerate of our feelings right away."
Nancy said it in a joking tone, but the moment she saw her sister’s face full of happiness, and then looked at Luis’s gentle expression.
Even though she knew she shouldn’t and wasn’t qualified, her heart felt sour with jealousy, extremely uncomfortable, especially unpleasant.
"Husband, let me help you."
"No need, I can handle it. Don’t you trust my skills?"
"I trust you, my husband’s cooking is the best. I’ll go change my clothes."

The mother and her two daughters changed into comfortable home clothes. Because Daniel was coming, all three of them wore bras, which was particularly ridiculous, especially since Nancy had promised just last night not to wear one at home anymore.
"You all go sit over there, don’t interfere with my performance."
The mother and two daughters started watching TV in the living room and even took out the almost never-used tea set to wash. After all, a guest is a guest, and certain formalities must be observed.
Lily couldn’t help but ask, "Elder Sister, is your mother-in-law coming to eat at our house too?"
Nancy snorted and said irritably, "In your dreams. I was thinking of just having a quick meal downstairs, but Mom said to eat at home."

Ruth said with a stern expression, "I’ve discussed it with your brother-in-law. The saying ’a doting mother ruins the son’ is their business. Our family has family traditions and upbringing; we can’t compete in a race to the bottom with others. No matter what, we must entertain them properly first."
The two sisters looked suddenly enlightened; no one knows a mother better than her daughter.

Heaven knows, Ruth is a standard shrew. Talking about family traditions and upbringing seems a bit laughable. Needless to say, it must have been Luis’s idea, since he is the head of the household now.
Nancy rolled her eyes and said, "Mom, then why didn’t you come back earlier to help buy groceries or assist a bit?"
"Exactly!"
Lily, feeling sorry for her husband, chimed in, "Skipping a little playing time won’t kill you. Even people clocking in for work aren’t as punctual as you."

Seeing the two sisters daring to criticize her, the mother tiger frowned and was about to assert her authority when Luis called out, "Mom, take one of your bracelets and give it to Elder Sister to wear."
"Don’t let them think our family is so poor. Everyone dress up nicely. It’s not like we can’t live without that Daniel."

This sentence saved the two sisters from dire straits and also ignited the competitive spirit and unity of the mother and three daughters. They immediately started chattering, discussing and swapping jewelry.
In the end, it was still too shabby. Apart from the three bracelets Luis bought, one for each, nothing else was really presentable.
The LV bag Nancy bought today for over 5,000 dollars was quite nice, but carrying a bag while eating is a bit conspicuous.
"They’re here!"
The doorbell rang, and the Wood mother and daughters acted as if facing a great enemy, even making some adjustments before opening the door.
Luis checked the time; it was exactly 5:30, one minute early. He had to admit, that woman Hela had an insanely strong, almost obsessive-compulsive sense of punctuality.
Told his mother-in-law they’d arrive at 5:30, and she actually showed up right on the dot. Living with such an obsessive-compulsive career woman must be miserable.
The door opened. Hela, dressed in high-end professional attire, had an exceptionally strong aura. She entered with a charming, bright smile, "Dear mother-in-law, we’re here."

Following behind was Daniel, who looked somewhat listless, nobody knew where he had been fooling around. He carried some fruit and two boxes of tea; probably wouldn’t have brought anything if his mother hadn’t told him to.
"Dear mother-in-law, please, come in, sit down. We’ll be eating shortly."
Ruth also received them with considerable poise. Hela, in her high-end business suit and gold-rimmed glasses, projected an overwhelming presence the moment she stepped in.
The calm demeanor of a highly educated woman who was clearly accustomed to feeling superior to others made Daniel seem rather foolish following behind her.
That authoritative aura caused Luis’s body to tense slightly, as he fantasized about how exhilarating it would be to press her down beneath him and wantonly humiliate her at will.

Daniel set down the items. Just then, Luis emerged from the kitchen wearing an apron, carrying a plate of roasted pork ribs in one hand and a bowl of steamed meat with egg in the other, placing them on the table.
Daniel saw it and laughed, "Luis, you’re quite the qualified live-in son-in-law. You’ve got real skill at serving your wife."
Hela acted as if she didn’t hear, but the Wood mother and daughters were now united, and their tempers had grown sharper too.
Ruth immediately snorted and said, "Yes, my second daughter is truly blessed. She married a man who knows how to care for others, understand warmth and cold, and cherish people."
The implication was very clear: my eldest daughter was unlucky to marry you.
"What prospects does a grown man have, doing housework all day at home?"
Daniel’s face instantly flushed red.
"Prospects like yours!"
Lily retorted coolly, "My husband didn’t pay a bride price, and neither did my brother-in-law. What’s the difference?"

chapters.title: Chapter 169: Sarcastic Battle
paragraphs: Hearing this, Daniel immediately became restless, "My family bought a wedding house! This guy just moved into your place with his luggage."
Hearing this, Nancy immediately cut her off, instead smiling cheerfully at Hela and saying, "Mother-in-law, that house is only in your son’s name, it has absolutely nothing to do with me, right?"
Asked this, Hela was first stunned, then her delicate brows furrowed. She had come to demand answers, but instead found the other party taking the offensive first.
"Well, it’s your marital home after all, how can you draw such clear lines?"
Hela said this as a mere formality.
But the current Nancy, free from psychological pressure, having inherited her mother’s shrewishness and the materialism of their social circle, wouldn’t swallow such toxic positivity.
"Mother-in-law is right. Did you hear that, Daniel?"
Nancy said lightly, "Transfer the property to me tomorrow."
Daniel could no longer sit still, his face turning ugly, "My parents paid for it, why should I transfer it to you?"
Nancy said with a smile, "Your mother said, family shouldn’t keep strict accounts. What’s the difference between what’s mine and what’s yours?"
"Look, Mother-in-law, your son treats what you say as bullshit."
Not only did she confront him directly, she then turned to look at her own mother-in-law and added in a sarcastic tone.
This soft, subtle jab was incredibly potent. Not only was Ruth’s face full of approval, even Luis nearly applauded her.
But starting off with such intense confrontation, how should the next part of the play continue?
Luis quickly stepped into the role of the peacemaker, saying, "Lily, Elder Sister, please help bring out the dishes. Let’s eat quickly."
He bought a few ready-made dishes, preparing a total of eight dishes and one soup. The soup black chicken soup, which was considered quite a lavish spread for a regular home-cooked meal.
Yet, Daniel arrived, and without even picking up his chopsticks, he stifled his anger and said, "Luis, you didn’t prepare any alcohol."
"Yes, I did!"
What Luis brought out was naturally his Mother-In-Law Ruth’s red wine.

Daniel immediately seized the opportunity to criticize, saying with disdain, "More of this fake stuff. Since you arranged the dinner tonight, couldn’t you make it a bit more upscale? Who are you looking down on?"
Luis didn’t even need to speak. His Mother-In-Law Ruth was the first to flare up.
In the past, when she was in her shrewish mode, she would have started cursing loudly. But under Luis’s strong psychological guidance, they had decided to fight fire with fire.
Ruth smiled cheerfully as she poured wine for Hela, saying, "Dear Mother-In-Law, we are just ordinary folks. We know your family is wealthy and we can’t compare."

"It’s normal for your son to always look down on my wine. But then again, I’ve never seen him bring a single bottle of real wine. Look how many years they’ve been married. Couldn’t he occasionally remember this and let us poor commoners get a glimpse of the good stuff?"
This was top-tier sarcasm, almost directly pointing at his nose and saying his son had no upbringing or manners.

Hela’s face instantly turned extremely ugly. Ruth’s combat ability was truly formidable. "Everyone says my daughter married well. I’d like to share in some of that glory too. Don’t mind my petty, commoner thinking."
"Wasn’t the wine Daniel brought for the New Year any good either?"
Hela’s expression immediately darkened a bit.

But Daniel’s face turned even uglier in an instant. Ruth, being quite shrewd, immediately feigned surprise and said, "For the New Year? For the New Year he just bought some fruit. There wasn’t any wine or tea or anything like that."
"What?"
Hela turned to look at her son, her voice sharp with anger. "Didn’t your father get a bottle of aged cognac and a carton of premium cigarettes for the New Year?"
Daniel immediately lowered his head guiltily. Ruth also looked shocked. "Mother-In-Law, no, there wasn’t."

Lily immediately added fuel to the fire, saying, "Yeah, for the New Year, brother-in-law just bought two bags of loose fruit without any packaging. Even the gifts people bring when visiting patients in the hospital aren’t that shabby."
Hearing this, Hela’s face instantly couldn’t hold up. She said sternly, "Daniel, what is the meaning of this?"
If it were about being stingy, Hela and her family valued face too much to be stingy. This didn’t seem like a coordinated act. The only possibility was that Daniel had kept the gifts for himself.
"Mom, I went out drinking that night, got really drunk, lost the stuff, so I didn’t bring it..."
Daniel explained guiltily.
By taking the blame, he at least gave Hela a way to save face.
Of course, not kicking someone when they’re down would make her an unqualified shrew. Ruth was in full combat mode today. She immediately put on an expression of sudden understanding and said,
"I see! I thought Mother-In-Llaw didn’t seem like someone without proper upbringing. How could she not teach him such basic manners?"
"Ah, you have no idea how upset I was. We’re poor, living in a relocation housing complex where all the neighbors know each other. Everyone was gossiping about it."

"Even when poor relatives from the countryside come for New Year, they at least bring a few live chickens. For the eldest son-in-law to show up with such pitiful gifts... I was too embarrassed to even leave the house for a while then."
"Daniel, you should have told me earlier. Look, Mother-In-Law has misunderstood you for so long."
Listening to this relentless stream of sarcasm, Luis felt particularly vindicated, silently admiring his Mother-In-Law’s formidable combat skills.
Even Nancy didn’t know about this matter, so it was almost certain that he had pocketed the gifts himself. Hela knew her son’s character all too well.
She was a little angry that her son hadn’t mentioned this, putting her at a disadvantage from the start.

So she could only put on a smile, raise her glass, and say, "Mother-In-Law, this is all a misunderstanding. We were afraid the young people wouldn’t know what to buy for New Year visits, so we prepared the gifts for them. Who knew he’d be so careless?"
"That’s right, young people are impulsive, it’s understandable."

Ruth, this top-tier fighter, wearing an expression of understanding, immediately added, "He hasn’t brought anything for the past two or three years. I’ve told him he’s this careless every year. This bad habit really needs to be corrected."
Hearing this, Hela’s hand, holding the wine glass, froze mid-air. Her face turned even uglier.
She paused for a moment, then turned to Nancy and said, "Nancy, why didn’t you tell me about this?"

Nancy said with a wronged expression, "I felt ashamed too. I mentioned it to Daniel, and he said that your family has high standards, and just him coming to pay New Year respects was giving enough face."
Hearing this, Hela’s face turned deathly pale.

Because no matter how much you look down on someone deep down, unless you’re openly breaking ties, you should at least maintain appearances. Otherwise, people aren’t looking down on Ruth, they’re looking down on the Zhang family for having no manners.
"I’ll ask for details when I get back!"
Hela felt intensely uncomfortable in that moment. Any expert would know how painful it is to come with accusations only to be preemptively shut down.
Daniel, seeing the situation turning sour, immediately said, "Let’s not talk about this for now."
"Better not to talk about it, it’s embarrassing to mention!"
Nancy took the wine glass in front of him and set it aside, saying nonchalantly, "Don’t drink this fake foreign wine. Next time, bring some genuine stuff for us to see."
Her attitude wasn’t exactly soft, but it wasn’t hard either. Yet, this was clearly more uncomfortable than an outright confrontation or flipping the table.

Daniel’s face was dark, but he didn’t dare to lose his temper. Gnashing his teeth, he said gloomily, "You should talk about yourself first. How did you end up with so much debt from your reckless spending?"
"I told you, those were scam calls."
Nancy looked at him calmly.
Daniel sneered, pulled out a piece of paper, and said, "I’ve written down all the debt collection calls during this time, which credit card, which platform, even the amounts owed."
Hearing this, Hela remembered the main issue and regained her composure. She immediately said to Ruth,

"Mother-In-Law, I think we should discuss this matter first. After all, the young couple’s life together is most important. But when problems arise, we as elders must still step in and discipline them if needed."
Ruth was initially startled, but seeing Luis calmly peeling shrimp for his wife Lily nearby, she instantly felt fully confident.
Ruth smiled gently and said, "Indeed, they are all our own children."
Hela immediately said with a sigh, "After they got married, Daniel’s business ventures kept failing. You know this too."
This was almost saying outright that her daughter was a jinx.

Ruth retorted without warmth or enthusiasm, "He hasn’t done business since getting married, right? He lost even more before marriage. Didn’t I hear you say he lost money in everything he did and almost jumped off a building?"
"Back then, Daniel even said he needed to check if the ancestral grave was affecting his wealth."
This was a veiled insult, yet it didn’t sound like one. The key was that Daniel had indeed said those things.
Hela was momentarily speechless. It was only then that she realized the shrew she viewed as uneducated and uncultured was, at least when it came to arguing, undeniably gifted.

Nancy said with a smile, "Your mother said, family shouldn’t keep strict accounts.
What’s the difference between what’s mine and what’s yours?"
"Look, Mother-in-law, your son treats what you say as bullshit."
Not only did she confront him directly, she then turned to look at her own mother-in-law and added in a sarcastic tone.
This soft, subtle jab was incredibly potent.
Not only was Ruth’s face full of approval, even Luis nearly applauded her.
But starting off with such intense confrontation, how should the next part of the play continue?
Luis quickly stepped into the role of the peacemaker, saying, "Lily, Elder Sister, please help bring out the dishes.
Let’s eat quickly."
He bought a few ready-made dishes, preparing a total of eight dishes and one soup.
The soup black chicken soup, which was considered quite a lavish spread for a regular home-cooked meal.
Yet, Daniel arrived, and without even picking up his chopsticks, he stifled his anger and said, "Luis, you didn’t prepare any alcohol."
"Yes, I did!"
What Luis brought out was naturally his Mother-In-Law Ruth’s red wine.
Daniel immediately seized the opportunity to criticize, saying with disdain, "More of this fake stuff.
Since you arranged the dinner tonight, couldn’t you make it a bit more upscale?
Who are you looking down on?"
Luis didn’t even need to speak.
His Mother-In-Law Ruth was the first to flare up.
In the past, when she was in her shrewish mode, she would have started cursing loudly.
But under Luis’s strong psychological guidance, they had decided to fight fire with fire.
Ruth smiled cheerfully as she poured wine for Hela, saying, "Dear Mother-In-Law, we are just ordinary folks.
We know your family is wealthy and we can’t compare."
"It’s normal for your son to always look down on my wine.
But then again, I’ve never seen him bring a single bottle of real wine.
Look how many years they’ve been married.
Couldn’t he occasionally remember this and let us poor commoners get a glimpse of the good stuff?"
This was top-tier sarcasm, almost directly pointing at his nose and saying his son had no upbringing or manners.
Hela’s face instantly turned extremely ugly.
Ruth’s combat ability was truly formidable.
"Everyone says my daughter married well.
I’d like to share in some of that glory too.
Don’t mind my petty, commoner thinking."
"Wasn’t the wine Daniel brought for the New Year any good either?"
Hela’s expression immediately darkened a bit.
But Daniel’s face turned even uglier in an instant.
Ruth, being quite shrewd, immediately feigned surprise and said, "For the New Year?
For the New Year he just bought some fruit.
There wasn’t any wine or tea or anything like that."
"What?"
Hela turned to look at her son, her voice sharp with anger.
"Didn’t your father get a bottle of aged cognac and a carton of premium cigarettes for the New Year?"
Daniel immediately lowered his head guiltily.
Ruth also looked shocked.
"Mother-In-Law, no, there wasn’t."
Lily immediately added fuel to the fire, saying, "Yeah, for the New Year, brother-in-law just bought two bags of loose fruit without any packaging.
Even the gifts people bring when visiting patients in the hospital aren’t that shabby."
Hearing this, Hela’s face instantly couldn’t hold up.
She said sternly, "Daniel, what is the meaning of this?"
If it were about being stingy, Hela and her family valued face too much to be stingy.
This didn’t seem like a coordinated act.
The only possibility was that Daniel had kept the gifts for himself.
"Mom, I went out drinking that night, got really drunk, lost the stuff, so I didn’t bring it..."
Daniel explained guiltily.
By taking the blame, he at least gave Hela a way to save face.
Of course, not kicking someone when they’re down would make her an unqualified shrew.
Ruth was in full combat mode today.
She immediately put on an expression of sudden understanding and said,
"I see!
I thought Mother-In-Llaw didn’t seem like someone without proper upbringing.
How could she not teach him such basic manners?"
"Ah, you have no idea how upset I was.
We’re poor, living in a relocation housing complex where all the neighbors know each other.
Everyone was gossiping about it."
"Even when poor relatives from the countryside come for New Year, they at least bring a few live chickens.
For the eldest son-in-law to show up with such pitiful gifts...
I was too embarrassed to even leave the house for a while then."
"Daniel, you should have told me earlier.
Look, Mother-In-Law has misunderstood you for so long."
Listening to this relentless stream of sarcasm, Luis felt particularly vindicated, silently admiring his Mother-In-Law’s formidable combat skills.
Even Nancy didn’t know about this matter, so it was almost certain that he had pocketed the gifts himself.
Hela knew her son’s character all too well.
She was a little angry that her son hadn’t mentioned this, putting her at a disadvantage from the start.
So she could only put on a smile, raise her glass, and say, "Mother-In-Law, this is all a misunderstanding.
We were afraid the young people wouldn’t know what to buy for New Year visits, so we prepared the gifts for them.
Who knew he’d be so careless?"
"That’s right, young people are impulsive, it’s understandable."
Ruth, this top-tier fighter, wearing an expression of understanding, immediately added, "He hasn’t brought anything for the past two or three years.
I’ve told him he’s this careless every year.
This bad habit really needs to be corrected."
Hearing this, Hela’s hand, holding the wine glass, froze mid-air.
Her face turned even uglier.
She paused for a moment, then turned to Nancy and said, "Nancy, why didn’t you tell me about this?"
Nancy said with a wronged expression, "I felt ashamed too.
I mentioned it to Daniel, and he said that your family has high standards, and just him coming to pay New Year respects was giving enough face."
Hearing this, Hela’s face turned deathly pale.
Because no matter how much you look down on someone deep down, unless you’re openly breaking ties, you should at least maintain appearances.
Otherwise, people aren’t looking down on Ruth, they’re looking down on the Zhang family for having no manners.
"I’ll ask for details when I get back!"
Hela felt intensely uncomfortable in that moment.
Any expert would know how painful it is to come with accusations only to be preemptively shut down.
Daniel, seeing the situation turning sour, immediately said, "Let’s not talk about this for now."
"Better not to talk about it, it’s embarrassing to mention!"
Nancy took the wine glass in front of him and set it aside, saying nonchalantly, "Don’t drink this fake foreign wine.
Next time, bring some genuine stuff for us to see."
Her attitude wasn’t exactly soft, but it wasn’t hard either.
Yet, this was clearly more uncomfortable than an outright confrontation or flipping the table.
Daniel’s face was dark, but he didn’t dare to lose his temper.
Gnashing his teeth, he said gloomily, "You should talk about yourself first.
How did you end up with so much debt from your reckless spending?"
"I told you, those were scam calls."
Nancy looked at him calmly.
Daniel sneered, pulled out a piece of paper, and said, "I’ve written down all the debt collection calls during this time, which credit card, which platform, even the amounts owed."
Hearing this, Hela remembered the main issue and regained her composure.
She immediately said to Ruth,
"Mother-In-Law, I think we should discuss this matter first.
After all, the young couple’s life together is most important.
But when problems arise, we as elders must still step in and discipline them if needed."
Ruth was initially startled, but seeing Luis calmly peeling shrimp for his wife Lily nearby, she instantly felt fully confident.
Ruth smiled gently and said, "Indeed, they are all our own children."
Hela immediately said with a sigh, "After they got married, Daniel’s business ventures kept failing.
You know this too."
This was almost saying outright that her daughter was a jinx.
Ruth retorted without warmth or enthusiasm, "He hasn’t done business since getting married, right?
He lost even more before marriage.
Didn’t I hear you say he lost money in everything he did and almost jumped off a building?"
"Back then, Daniel even said he needed to check if the ancestral grave was affecting his wealth."
This was a veiled insult, yet it didn’t sound like one.
The key was that Daniel had indeed said those things.
Hela was momentarily speechless.
It was only then that she realized the shrew she viewed as uneducated and uncultured was, at least when it came to arguing, undeniably gifted.

chapters.title: Chapter 170: Daniel Crumbling
paragraphs: "Wife, you should drink more of this soup, it is very nourishing!" Luis simply tended to his wife while also watching the drama unfold. Lily knew his confrontational skills weren’t strong, so it was best not to hold him back. The couple shared a tacit smile, filled with tender affection.

"Since they got married, they haven’t held proper jobs. We’ve been subsidizing their water, electricity, gas, and living expenses. Nancy hasn’t found a steady job either. She occasionally talks about part time work, but it never earns much money."
"We wouldn’t dare to boast, but let’s just say we’re neither rich nor poor. Even without working, we could support them."
"But owing so much money, it just doesn’t make sense!"
Hela adjusted her posture and spoke with grave sincerity. "Mother in law, as her mother, you really should get to the bottom of this."
"There’s such a thing?" Ruth looked genuinely surprised, her acting utterly convincing.
Hela brought out a bag she had with her. Upon opening it, it was full of jewelry boxes.
She then said, "Mother in law, to be perfectly honest, when Nancy got married, the ’Three Golds’, including the gold jewelry given by relatives, were worth nearly 10,000 dollars."
"I heard she sold some of it before. What’s left with me is only worth about 5,000 dollars now."
"She even sold the gold jewelry?" Ruth took the bag and looked inside, exclaiming with a convincingly shocked expression.

Daniel stopped pretending at this point and stated bluntly, "Mom, occasionally when I maxed out my credit cards, my parents paid them off. I also received living expenses. But Nancy spends so extravagantly all the time, that when she couldn’t cover it before, she sold the gold jewelry."
"If she was just lazy at home, fine, I could support that. But I can’t stand her constant comparing herself to others all the time."
The atmosphere was so tense you could cut it with a knife. The six people at the table had barely picked up their chopsticks ten times before the battle lines were drawn. It was truly a spectacle.
Nancy sneered coldly. "Is that so? All the cigarettes and things I bought for you might as well have been fed to a dog."
Daniel’s face turned stern. "We are discussing the significant debts you’ve accumulated right now."

Hela also spoke with apparent sincerity. "Mother in law, to be frank, Daniel’s father and I are currently a bit short on funds ourselves. Regarding this matter, you will need to provide the support yourselves. I’ve brought the remaining gold jewelry here."
"More than that I cannot manage, but I can scrape together twenty or thirty thousand dollars..."
Twenty or thirty thousand dollars was likely a significant sum for Daniel and Nancy, but for her, it was absolutely not. This was purely meant to be insulting.
It was almost like pointing a finger and shouting, ’What kind of daughter have you raised? A useless vase, lazy and greedy, buried in debt, and she had the audacity to expose my shortcomings first.’
"Nancy, how could you possibly owe so much money?" Ruth’s acting was superb, immediately switching to a look of bitter disappointment directed at Nancy.
Although she had little prior information, Luis had already started serving his beloved wife more food. His calm demeanor was enough to bolster her confidence.

Nancy simply moved to sit between the two of them, snorted haughtily, and said, "I told you it was a scam text message. I may not have a regular job, but the money I earn from part time work means I at least have some savings."
"Then how do you explain this?" Daniel produced his compiled list of incriminating evidence: the various lending platforms and the amounts owed.
Nancy looked at him with a cold sneer, took out her phone, opened Whatsapp, and said, "Mother in law, the WetLoan is about twenty thousand dollars, correct?"
She opened the corresponding app interface. Daniel leaned in to look and was dumbfounded.
Forget the credit limit or outstanding balance; the function itself had been deactivated. Meaning, without even having a credit line, it was impossible to have borrowed money.
"Impossible! Then there’s also..." Daniel began to panic as he saw this.
For each platform he named, Nancy opened the corresponding app right in front of her mother and mother in law. Every single online lending platform showed its services deactivated.
If there was an outstanding debt, you couldn’t close the account. Or, if it wasn’t activated, you couldn’t borrow money in the first place.
"Impossible, impossible! You have credit cards! I’ve seen those credit card statements!"
Nancy directly opened her credit card app and showed the screen to her mother in law, Hela.
Daniel immediately exploded. "This one I know! This one has the most debt, over forty thousand dollars!!"
"You bastard!!" Hela was also furious because the screen showed a zero balance owed, with an available credit limit of forty five thousand dollars.
Daniel snatched the phone away, staring at it while saying, "This can’t be right! I saw her take out many loans!"
"Nancy, what is going on? You’ve been borrowing money?" Ruth was already feeling reassured by now, but the performance had to continue, so she asked immediately.
"Nonsense, if I had to rely on him and his parents begging for food, I would have starved to death long ago. I’m not some frumpy housewife, at least I need to buy cosmetics and things like that."

Nancy was now holding her head high with pride, scolding, "Those part-time gigs as an etiquette hostess are exhausting, standing all day. He comes home, plays games, then goes out drinking at night. I had to start my own little business, otherwise if his parents stopped supporting us, I’d literally starve to death."
Hearing this, Daniel’s face turned particularly ugly.
Nancy was even more blunt, "Mother-in-law, only country bumpkins with no looks have to put up with that kind of hardship. You spend more on cosmetics than I do, you should understand me."
"That was a misunderstanding, a misunderstanding!"
Hela became somewhat flustered, probably not expecting a scene like this.

Daniel was completely furious, slamming the table and yelling, "You pig-brained idiot, what business are you running? Doing multi-level marketing like your mom, pushing these fake red wines, right? You’ll be lucky if you don’t lose your shirt."
This was too much, even Hela felt it was excessive; you shouldn’t say such things, even when drunk and causing trouble.
Ruth sneered coldly but didn’t speak. This shrew not speaking was somehow even more intimidating.

Nancy was no longer holding back either, lashing out, "Daniel, you’re just picking a fight, aren’t you? You can’t even talk properly, and now you’re insulting my mom? How much money did my mom’s multi-level marketing ever cost you?
"It’s fine, his family’s upbringing is probably just like that."
"After all, what kind of son-in-law comes for a New Year’s visit bringing two bags of bulk fruit? Even a live-in son-in-law spends a few thousand on gifts."
The atmosphere froze into an icy silence with that one sentence. Luis looked at his wife Lily with new respect.
Usually such a quiet person, but when she finally spoke, her soft, gentle words could cut deep. She never spoke unless it was shocking.
Hela’s expression was already extremely ugly, but she still pulled Daniel down to sit, angrily saying, "Shut up! How can you speak to your mother-in-law like that?"
It proved her authority was still strong; after all, she controlled Daniel’s financial lifeline, so her word carried weight.
Hela took a deep breath, immediately adopting a tone of concerned elder, "Nancy, then why did you sell the gold jewelry?"

"Money isn’t easy to come by these days. It’s easier to build a fortune than to keep it. Never mind making it grow, just preserving its value is an achievement. Gold is the best for preserving value right now, why sell it off just like that?"
It was clear she wasn’t giving up, planning to attack from a different angle.
"Oh, that sold for five thousand dollars!"
Nancy was completely unfazed, and started fiddling with her phone again. This made Hela’s heart sink.

Then Nancy pulled up a transfer record and showed it, saying, "This one thousand dollars, Daniel said it was for a friend transferring a set of game equipment, that he could make at least three to five hundred off it."
"But I never saw that three or five hundred, didn’t even see the original one thousand dollar principal back."
She had spent the whole night cleaning up her phone, keeping all the useful information and resolving all the bank collection notices.

Hela’s face darkened as soon as she saw it. Daniel quickly explained, "Mom, that equipment is all in my account. It’s still worth that much if I sell it now, the appreciation just wasn’t as much as I thought."
The excuse was pathetic; it was obvious he’d just spent the money on game gear and lied to his wife.
"And the remaining money?"
Hela asked again.
Ruth knew it was her time to step in. She immediately furrowed her delicate brows and asked, "Mother-in-law, your family isn’t that hard up, is it?"
This was a direct attack. Hela was stunned for a moment, then forced a smile and said, "Mother-in-law, what kind of talk is that?"
Ruth was not holding back at all now, "We sold it for five thousand dollars, spent over a thousand on your son. Your family didn’t give a betrothal gift, and we didn’t say anything."
"But I didn’t marry my daughter off to be a slave or a servant in your house. Why the inquisition over this bit of gold jewelry?"

chapters.title: Chapter 171: Beaten By Mother And Mother In Law
paragraphs: "Three thousand dollars, is it going to kill your family, or did you spend a fortune on it?"
"If you can’t afford a wife, just say so. Why are you lecturing her as if my daughter stole your money?"
Ruth, this shrew, was eloquent to begin with, and now, having the moral high ground, her output was devastatingly effective:
"Mother-in-law, that’s not how you should put it. What woman would sell her own jewelry unless she was truly desperate?"
"If Daniel were more capable, my daughter wouldn’t have to do this."

The words were deeply offensive, yet they weren’t baseless. Hela gritted her teeth and said, "Mother-in-law, I didn’t mean it that way. You said yourself it was her nest egg. I just wanted to show I care about them."

Ruth wasn’t having any of it, firing back immediately, "Mother-in-law, parents show they care by spending money and effort, not just with empty words. If you truly cared, you’d have known where Daniel spent that over a thousand dollars long ago."
"It’s for game equipment! It’s still worth that much if I sell it now!"
Seeing his mother losing ground repeatedly, Daniel’s anger flared, "And her? Where did that over three thousand dollars go? All those bottles and jars of cosmetics?"
"Since when do you control how I spend my money? How amusing."
Nancy smiled, raised her wrist, and said, "Mom, how much is this worth? The receipt is here, see for yourself."
The Summer Cicada series bracelet worth over three thousand dollars perfectly explained it away.
Daniel’s face changed, and he immediately said, "No, that’s your mother’s..."
Ruth raised her own hand and took Lily’s hand, saying speechlessly, "We’re wearing ours."
Lily even added, "Brother-in-law, one bracelet is enough. It’s not like you’re practicing Iron Wire Fist, you don’t need to wear so many."
Lily’s follow-up strikes were exceptionally precise. Normally, one would only buy one bracelet; who would have thought Luis bought two specifically to suck up.
Hela’s face was now full of helplessness. She said softly, "Nancy, what made you think of buying this?"
"That old jewelry was too tacky, I didn’t want to wear it anymore. I thought I’d buy something nice."
Nancy said as if it were the most natural thing in the world, "Mother-in-law, gold holds its value. I just spent a little on the craftsmanship fee. What’s the problem?"
"Well, you should have said so earlier, to avoid misunderstandings!"
Hela was mortified, feeling she had lost all face.
At the very least, everyone now knew the Daniels family’s contemptuous attitude. Ruth naturally wouldn’t let the opportunity slip, immediately adding,
"Mother-in-law, what exactly is wrong with your Daniel? He doesn’t earn money himself, yet he spends it on games."

"I won’t comment on other things, but if it were me, I certainly wouldn’t agree to this. Besides, the over three thousand dollars came from selling her own jewelry. What’s with the endless interrogation? It’s not his money."
"Even if your son mortgaged or sold the house, my daughter wouldn’t have the right to question it, would she?"
After this barrage, Hela felt utterly miserable, glaring fiercely at her son. This was completely different from what he had said before they came.
Daniel was already furious with humiliation. He suddenly pulled out another envelope and said, "Then what about this lawyer’s letter?
Nancy did not even glance at it. She directly tossed the contract to her mother-in-law, Hela, with a clever, radiant smile. "Mother, see for yourself!"
Her attitude was so detached that Hela instead grew timid. Not daring to open the contract, she asked, "What is the meaning of this?"
"Your son does not earn money, and you support him. I earn my own money and encountered some trouble. I did not want to worry you all. Who knew he would make such a tremendous fuss over nothing."
"As a husband, he is not only useless in helping, but now he is here causing more trouble. He is truly a piece of work."

Nancy now spoke lightly, yet her presence was overwhelmingly powerful. She stated directly, "All he knows is eating, drinking, and having fun. Mother-in-law, you ought to know that a lawyer’s letter is just a worthless piece of paper."
"Bullshit! It says right here that you have to pay tens of thousands!" Daniel immediately spat out, exasperated.

Nancy looked at him with utter contempt. "My apologies, but I have sued them as well. A few thousand is a conservative figure; you could write it as hundred of thousands. The real question is whether the court will support such a claim."
Hela felt a wave of weakness wash over her. Looking at her son, red-faced with shame and anger, she suddenly felt very angry herself.
Ruth suddenly let out a sigh and said, "Mother-in-law, if you look down on us, you can say it directly. There is no need to find so many excuses."
"Mother-in-law, you misunderstand me. I am also a parent; I do not mean that at all," Hela quickly said, resorting to polite, formal words.
"Last time, when the two children ended up at the police station, I thought you came to apologize as you said. Instead, you came to pick faults with our family."
Ruth, now holding the upper hand, immediately adopted a tone of helplessness. "Well then, you and Daniel should ponder what other faults you can possibly voice."
"He hit his wife, and yet he comes here saying these things. Bullying our family is not done this way."

"Mother, please say no more about this." Lily’s follow-up strike was particularly sharp. "Their family upbringing might be like gold and jade on the outside, but rotten within. Showing up empty-handed with New Year greetings for the mother-in-law’s family, only to express disdain upon arrival. After beating his wife, he fabricates stories and comes to our door to make trouble."
"Look down on our family? But I have never seen our elder brother-in-law buy anything for you. Perhaps he is too poor and has spent all his money, so he can only come to our house to put on a show."
"The elder son-in-law is less thoughtful than the second son-in-law who married into the family. Even a normal son-in-law from the countryside would not be that shabby." 2
"At the very least, he should bring a couple of local chickens, right? How can he just buy two random bags of fruit downstairs?"
"And as it happens, we know the fruit seller. Those two bags together cost less than 3 dollars, and he still picked the cheapest ones. The humiliation is monumental."
This comment made Hela’s face completely lose its composure, her expression shifting between dark and stormy one moment and clear the next.
At that moment, Daniel suddenly stood up, slammed the table, and shouted, "Lily, you ugly woman, shut your mouth for me! You have no sense of respect, who gave you the right to speak?"
"Shut up!" Hela spun around abruptly and slapped Daniel across the face.
The sound was exceptionally sharp and clear. Daniel covered his mouth as he sat down, his face a picture of disbelief. After a moment’s thought, he lowered his head again.
But he still roared unwillingly, "Mom, don’t listen to her nonsense! She sold all of her own bags! She must have..."
Before he could finish, Nancy sneered, took a newly bought bag from the coat rack beside her, and first placed an invoice in front of her mother-in-law.
"Mother-in-law, even if I sold three bags, they wouldn’t be worth much. The ones your son bought for me... well, it seems none are as good as the one you carry, are they?"

Not waiting for Hela to formulate a response, Nancy pointed at the new bag she had bought that day and said, "After selling them, I added my own money to buy a new one. That shouldn’t be considered excessive, should it? There’s really no need to come here and make an issue out of this."
"This... It’s not excessive!" Hela’s voice trembled slightly as she spoke.
"Your family spends money on your son. How stressful buying a house is has nothing to do with me. My name isn’t on that deed at all."

"Every day he nags at me about how stressful buying a house is. Is he insane? What does that have to do with me? If I had known about Daniel’s pile of gambling debts back when we got married, I would never have married him."

"And what’s the deal with your son’s living expenses? If he gets all the money, then why should I have to beg him for it like a beggar? Am I just a haggard housewife who only needs to avoid starvation each month?"
Nancy completely erupted now. She slammed the table and stood up, saying, "Mother-in-law, are these matters clear now?"
"Clear, clear!" Hela was also startled.
This was the first time Nancy had lost her temper in front of her.
"If it’s not clear, it doesn’t matter. You didn’t contribute a single cent. What does it matter to you whether it’s clear or not?"
"Understood. If she really owed 20,000 dollars, how much would you contribute? Have you ever treated my elder sister as part of your family?"
"Changing a bag, changing a piece of gold jewelry, and you all stare like thieves. How poor must you be to be so sensitive?"
With this stab from Lily, Daniel and his mother were suffocated, while the Wood family members were mentally exhilarated.
Luis immediately brought a bowl of clear conch and fish maw soup from the kitchen and scolded mockingly, "Wife, the adults are talking. Don’t interrupt."
"Okay, I know~" The couple exchanged a secret chuckle.
Luis appeared to be stopping her, but in reality, he was rewarding her!
The atmosphere fell into a momentary silence. Hela simply did not know what to say.
She had originally intended to speak from a position of moral superiority, but instead found herself rebutted at every turn and was nearly driven mad.
"Daniel, how are we going to account for that slap you gave me?" Nancy asked, her face flushed with anger.
Hela immediately started, "Nancy, husband and wife fight at the head of the bed and make up at the foot. It’s normal."
Her words immediately drew dissatisfaction from Ruth.
"That was in the past. Who can tolerate such treatment nowadays? Mother-in-law, look at what happened today. Your son deliberately created all this messy trouble to pick on Nancy, isn’t that right?"
"What, if your husband hit you, would you endure it? If it were me, I definitely wouldn’t."
"The hitting is done. You came here not to apologize but to say all this. Think for yourself whether there is any sincerity in that."
Hela was also losing patience. "Mother-in-law, then what do you suggest we do?"
"What to do?!" Nancy was a fiery character too. The moment her mother-in-law’s words fell, she suddenly stepped forward and slapped Daniel hard across the face.
